"""Launch the bundled Miles fully-async GRPO trainer on the public workload.

Topology, model and rollout settings live in ``scripts/run_config.json``; this
file only turns them into the Miles command line, starts any local services the
rollout needs, and records the exact launch in ``experiment_logs/<run>/``.

    python3 scripts/train_reproduction.py                 # full run
    python3 scripts/train_reproduction.py --print-command # show the trainer argv
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import shlex
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

WORKSPACE = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


def model_args(cfg: dict) -> list[str]:
    """Megatron shape arguments, derived from the HF config of the prepared model."""
    hf = json.loads((WORKSPACE / cfg["model"]["path"] / "config.json").read_text())
    text = hf.get("text_config", hf)
    args = [
        "--spec", "miles_plugins.models.qwen3_5", "get_qwen3_5_spec",
        "--disable-bias-linear", "--qk-layernorm", "--group-query-attention",
        "--num-attention-heads", str(text["num_attention_heads"]),
        "--num-query-groups", str(text["num_key_value_heads"]),
        "--kv-channels", str(text["head_dim"]),
        "--num-layers", str(text["num_hidden_layers"]),
        "--hidden-size", str(text["hidden_size"]),
        "--normalization", "RMSNorm", "--apply-layernorm-1p", "--position-embedding-type", "rope",
        "--norm-epsilon", str(text.get("rms_norm_eps", 1e-6)),
        "--rotary-percent", str(text.get("rope_parameters", text).get("partial_rotary_factor", 0.25)),
        "--rotary-base", str(int(text.get("rope_parameters", text).get("rope_theta", 10_000_000))),
        "--swiglu", "--untie-embeddings-and-output-weights", "--vocab-size", str(text["vocab_size"]),
        "--attention-output-gate",
    ]
    if text.get("num_experts"):
        layers = text["num_hidden_layers"]
        args += [
            "--ffn-hidden-size", str(text["moe_intermediate_size"]),
            "--moe-ffn-hidden-size", str(text["moe_intermediate_size"]),
            "--moe-shared-expert-intermediate-size", str(text["shared_expert_intermediate_size"]),
            "--moe-router-score-function", "softmax", "--moe-router-topk", str(text["num_experts_per_tok"]),
            "--moe-layer-freq", f"[1]*{layers}", "--num-experts", str(text["num_experts"]),
            "--moe-grouped-gemm", "--moe-token-drop-policy", "probs", "--moe-router-dtype", "fp32",
            "--moe-permute-fusion", "--moe-aux-loss-coeff", "0", "--moe-shared-expert-gate",
            "--moe-token-dispatcher-type", "alltoall",
        ]
    else:
        args += ["--ffn-hidden-size", str(text["intermediate_size"])]
    return args


def torch_dist_dir(cfg: dict) -> Path:
    return WORKSPACE / (cfg["model"]["path"] + "_torch_dist")


def convert_checkpoint(cfg: dict, env: dict, log_dir: Path) -> None:
    """One-time HF -> Megatron torch_dist conversion (offline, on the task GPUs)."""
    target = torch_dist_dir(cfg)
    if (target / "latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt").is_file():
        return
    conv = cfg["conversion"]
    argv = [sys.executable, "-m", "torch.distributed.run", "--nproc-per-node", str(conv["gpus"]),
            "scripts/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py", *model_args(cfg),
            # Shard the conversion by pipeline stage, never by expert: mbridge's loader for the
            # fused 3-D expert tensors of the public checkpoint ignores the expert-parallel offset,
            # so with EP>1 every rank would load experts 0..E/EP-1. Training reshards on load.
            "--tensor-model-parallel-size", "1", "--pipeline-model-parallel-size", str(conv["pp"]),
            "--expert-model-parallel-size", "1", "--expert-tensor-parallel-size", "1",
            "--seq-length", "4096", "--max-position-embeddings", "4096", "--bf16",
            "--rollout-batch-size", "1",  # required by the Miles argument set; unused here
            "--hf-checkpoint", str(WORKSPACE / cfg["model"]["path"]), "--save", str(target)]
    (log_dir / "convert_command.json").write_text(json.dumps(argv, indent=2) + "\n")
    with open(log_dir / "convert.log", "ab") as log:
        rc = subprocess.call(argv, cwd=WORKSPACE, env=env, stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    if rc != 0 or not (target / "latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt").is_file():
        raise RuntimeError(f"checkpoint conversion failed (exit {rc}); see {log_dir / 'convert.log'}")


def build_command(cfg: dict) -> list[str]:
    topo, roll, train, router = cfg["topology"], cfg["rollout"], cfg["training"], cfg["router"]
    model = str(WORKSPACE / cfg["model"]["path"])
    argv = [
        sys.executable, "scripts/native_entrypoint.py",
        "--train-backend", "megatron",
        "--actor-num-nodes", "1", "--actor-num-gpus-per-node", str(topo["actor_gpus"]),
        "--rollout-num-gpus", str(topo["rollout_gpus"]),
        "--rollout-num-gpus-per-engine", str(topo["rollout_gpus_per_engine"]),
        "--num-gpus-per-node", str(topo["actor_gpus"] + topo["rollout_gpus"]),
        "--hf-checkpoint", model, "--ref-load", str(torch_dist_dir(cfg)), "--bf16",
        *model_args(cfg),
        "--seq-length", str(roll["max_context_len"]), "--max-position-embeddings", str(roll["max_context_len"]),
        "--tensor-model-parallel-size", str(train["tp"]), "--pipeline-model-parallel-size", "1",
        "--context-parallel-size", "1", "--expert-model-parallel-size", str(train["ep"]),
        "--expert-tensor-parallel-size", "1",
        "--recompute-granularity", "full", "--recompute-method", "uniform", "--recompute-num-layers", "1",
        "--use-dynamic-batch-size", "--max-tokens-per-gpu", str(train["max_tokens_per_gpu"]),
        # 248k-entry vocabulary: never materialize [tokens, vocab] logits
        "--fused-logprob", "--log-probs-max-tokens-per-gpu", str(train["log_probs_max_tokens_per_gpu"]),
        "--advantage-estimator", "grpo", "--entropy-coef", "0", "--eps-clip", "0.2", "--eps-clip-high", "0.28",
        "--optimizer", "adam", "--lr", str(train["lr"]), "--lr-decay-style", "constant",
        "--weight-decay", "0.1", "--adam-beta1", "0.9", "--adam-beta2", "0.98",
        "--attention-dropout", "0.0", "--hidden-dropout", "0.0",
        "--attention-softmax-in-fp32", "--attention-backend", "flash",
        "--rollout-function-path", "runtime.rollout.generate_rollout",
        "--custom-generate-function-path", "runtime.agent_generate.generate",
        # Generate-function options reach the legacy rollout path through Miles'
        # --custom-config-path YAML (written next to the run logs by main()).
        "--custom-config-path", "{custom_config}",
        "--prompt-data", str(WORKSPACE / roll["data"]), "--input-key", "messages", "--label-key", "label",
        "--metadata-key", "metadata", "--rollout-shuffle", "--rollout-seed", "20261116",
        "--num-rollout", str(roll["num_rollout"]), "--rollout-batch-size", str(roll["batch_groups"]),
        "--n-samples-per-prompt", str(roll["samples_per_group"]),
        "--global-batch-size", str(roll["batch_groups"] * roll["samples_per_group"]),
        "--rollout-max-response-len", str(roll["max_new_tokens_per_turn"]),
        "--rollout-max-context-len", str(roll["max_context_len"]),
        "--rollout-temperature", "1.0", "--rollout-top-p", "1.0",
        "--sglang-mem-fraction-static", str(roll["sglang_mem_fraction"]),
        "--sglang-server-concurrency", str(roll["server_concurrency"]),
        "--update-weights-interval", "1", "--pause-generation-mode", "abort",
        "--custom-megatron-before-train-step-hook-path", "runtime.training_evidence.observe_train_step",
        "--no-use-prometheus-scrape",
    ]
    if train.get("fused_logprob_seq_chunk_size"):
        argv += ["--fused-logprob-seq-chunk-size", str(train["fused_logprob_seq_chunk_size"])]
    if train.get("grads_in_fp32", True):
        argv += ["--accumulate-allreduce-grads-in-fp32"]
    if train.get("optimizer_cpu_offload"):
        argv += ["--optimizer-cpu-offload", "--use-precision-aware-optimizer"]
        if train.get("overlap_cpu_optimizer_transfers", False):
            argv += ["--overlap-cpu-optimizer-d2h-h2d"]
    if train["tp"] > 1:
        argv += ["--sequence-parallel"]
    if router.get("use_miles_router"):
        argv += ["--use-miles-router"]
    if router.get("policy"):
        argv += ["--sglang-router-policy", router["policy"]]
    return argv + cfg.get("extra_args", [])


def start_services(cfg: dict, env: dict, log_dir: Path) -> list[subprocess.Popen]:
    procs = []
    for svc in cfg.get("services", []):
        cmd = [sys.executable, *[a.replace("{log_dir}", str(log_dir)) for a in svc["argv"]]]
        out = open(log_dir / f"{svc['name']}.log", "ab")
        procs.append(subprocess.Popen(cmd, cwd=WORKSPACE, env=env, stdout=out, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT))
        url = svc.get("health_url")
        for _ in range(120):
            if url is None:
                break
            try:
                import urllib.request

                # local service: never route the probe through a host proxy
                urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.ProxyHandler({})).open(url, timeout=2)
                break
            except Exception:
                time.sleep(0.5)
        else:
            raise RuntimeError(f"service {svc['name']} did not become healthy")
    return procs


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--print-command", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--config", type=Path, default=WORKSPACE / "scripts/run_config.json")
    options, extra = parser.parse_known_args()
    cfg = json.loads(options.config.read_text())
    argv = build_command(cfg) + extra
    if options.print_command:
        print(shlex.join(argv))
        return 0
    run_name = time.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ", time.gmtime()) + f"-{os.getpid()}"
    # The harness collects $AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs; a manual launch logs into the workspace.
    log_root = Path(os.environ["AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS"]) if os.environ.get("AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS") else WORKSPACE
    log_dir = log_root / "experiment_logs" / run_name
    log_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    custom_config = log_dir / "generate_args.yaml"
    custom_config.write_text(json.dumps({
        "generate_max_turns": cfg["rollout"]["max_turns"],
        "generate_tool_call_parser": cfg["rollout"]["tool_call_parser"],
    }, indent=2) + "\n")
    argv = [str(custom_config) if a == "{custom_config}" else a for a in argv]
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["PYTHONPATH"] = os.pathsep.join([str(WORKSPACE / "vendor"), str(WORKSPACE), env.get("PYTHONPATH", "")])
    env.update({k: str(v) for k, v in cfg.get("env", {}).items()})
    env["FORWARD_ENV"] = ",".join(sorted(cfg.get("env", {})))
    env.update(RUN_EVIDENCE_DIR=str(log_dir), PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE="1", NO_VCS_VERSION="1",
               TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM="false", CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS="1", WANDB_MODE="disabled",
               PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF="expandable_segments:True")
    (log_dir / "launch.json").write_text(json.dumps(
        {"argv": argv, "config": cfg, "env": {k: env[k] for k in sorted(cfg.get("env", {}))}}, indent=2) + "\n")
    convert_checkpoint(cfg, env, log_dir)
    procs = start_services(cfg, env, log_dir)
    try:
        with open(log_dir / "train.log", "ab") as log:
            trainer = subprocess.Popen(argv, cwd=WORKSPACE, env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
            for line in trainer.stdout:
                sys.stdout.buffer.write(line)
                sys.stdout.flush()
                log.write(line)
            return trainer.wait()
    finally:
        for proc in procs:
            proc.send_signal(signal.SIGTERM)
            try:
                proc.wait(timeout=20)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                proc.kill()


if __name__ == "__main__":

# Asynchronous agentic GRPO workspace

`python3 -B scripts/train_reproduction.py` launches the bundled Miles
fully-asynchronous trainer (Ray + Megatron + SGLang) on a single 8-GPU node:
4 GPUs train the policy (expert-parallel 4, optimizer state offloaded to CPU) and 4 GPUs serve it as two tensor-parallel-2 SGLang engines. The policy is `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B`, fetched by the prepare stage into `models/`.
`--print-command` prints the exact trainer command line without running it.

The workload is `data/public_repo_tasks.jsonl`, 512 synthetic Python
repositories with one planted defect each, regenerated by the prepare stage
with `scripts/build_public_tasks.py`. The policy debugs them with tools
(`list_files`, `read_file`, `search`, `run_tests`, `submit_fix`) over up
to eight turns and is rewarded for naming the defective file and function
(a correct answer loses 0.05 per model turn beyond the second, floor 0.5).
Tools are computed from the repository carried in each sample and take sandbox-like time (seeded, log-normal around 0.4–3 s per call).

## Layout

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `scripts/train_reproduction.py`, `scripts/run_config.json` | launcher and its topology / rollout / training configuration |
| `scripts/native_entrypoint.py`, `runtime/source/train_async_entrypoint.py` | local Ray bootstrap and the Miles async training driver |
| `runtime/rollout.py`, `runtime/fully_async.py` | rollout function: continuous producer, group collection, recycling |
| `runtime/agent_generate.py`, `runtime/environment.py`, `runtime/repo_tools.py` | multi-turn generate function, per-trajectory environment, tools and reward |
| `runtime/training_evidence.py` | before-train-step hook that records every optimizer update |
| `vendor/` | Miles, Miles plugins and Megatron (Core, Bridge) Python source |
| `logs/historical/` | sanitized console logs and derived metrics of the original 16-GPU runs |
| `logs/public_rerun/` | outputs of one run of this workspace on 8 × H800 (layout as below; host names and paths replaced) |
| `scripts/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py` | one-time Hugging Face to Megatron checkpoint conversion run by the launcher |

## Outputs

Each launch writes `experiment_logs/<UTC time>-<pid>/`: `launch.json` (argv and
configuration), `train.log` (full console log), `rollout.<id>.json` (per-rollout
summary), `optimizer/step.<rollout>.<step>.rank<r>.json` (update identity, grad
norm, sampled parameter delta), `turns/*.jsonl` (one record per engine call and
tool batch).

the initial weight sync, and then overlaps rollout `k+1` with training on
rollout `k`, syncing weights after every update.

import copy
import logging
import multiprocessing
import random
import uuid

from sglang_router.launch_router import RouterArgs

from miles.rollout.session.server import run_session_server
from miles.router.router import run_router as run_miles_router
from miles.utils.http_utils import _wrap_ipv6, find_available_port, get_host_info, is_port_available
from miles.utils.http_utils import run_router as run_sglang_router
from miles.utils.http_utils import wait_for_server_ready

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def start_router(args, *, has_pd_disaggregation: bool = False, force_new: bool = False) -> tuple[str, int]:
    """Start sgl router or miles router and return (router_ip, router_port).

    If ``args.sglang_router_ip`` is already set and ``force_new`` is False,
    skip launching and return the existing values.
    """
    if not force_new and args.sglang_router_ip is not None:
        return args.sglang_router_ip, args.sglang_router_port

    router_ip = _wrap_ipv6(get_host_info()[1])
    if force_new:
        router_port = find_available_port(random.randint(3000, 4000))
    else:
        router_port = args.sglang_router_port
        if router_port is None:
            router_port = find_available_port(random.randint(3000, 4000))

    if args.use_miles_router:
        assert not has_pd_disaggregation, "miles router does not support PD disaggregation."

        run_router = run_miles_router
        router_args = copy.copy(args)
        router_args.sglang_router_ip = router_ip
        router_args.sglang_router_port = router_port

    else:
        run_router = run_sglang_router
        router_args = RouterArgs.from_cli_args(args, use_router_prefix=True)
        router_args.host = router_ip
        router_args.port = router_port
        router_args.prometheus_port = find_available_port(random.randint(4000, 5000))
        router_args.log_level = "warn"
        router_args.request_timeout_secs = args.sglang_router_request_timeout_secs

        if args.sglang_router_policy:
            router_args.policy = args.sglang_router_policy

        if has_pd_disaggregation:
            router_args.pd_disaggregation = True

        logger.info(f"Launch router with args: {router_args}")

    port = router_port
    if not is_port_available(port):
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Port {port} is already in use — a stale router process may still be running. "
            f"Run 'pkill -9 python' to kill it, then retry."
        )

    # spawn (not fork): the child must not inherit threads/finalizers from this
    # Ray actor (e.g. wandb's service thread), which deadlock a forked child.
    process = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process(
        target=run_router,
        args=(router_args,),
    )
    process.daemon = True
    process.start()
    wait_for_server_ready(router_ip, router_port, process, timeout=30)
    logger.info(f"Router launched at {router_ip}:{router_port}")
    return router_ip, router_port


def _resolve_session_server_ports(raw: list[int] | None) -> list[int]:
    """Resolve the ``--session-server-port`` value into the ports to serve on.

    None: one auto-allocated port. One value: a single server on that port.
    Two values: the half-open range [start, end), one server per port.
    """
    if raw is None:
        return [find_available_port(random.randint(5000, 6000))]
    if len(raw) == 1:
        return raw
    if len(raw) == 2:
        start, end = raw
        if start >= end:
            raise ValueError(f"--session-server-port range [{start}, {end}) is empty.")
        return list(range(start, end))
    raise ValueError(f"--session-server-port takes one port or a start/end range, got {len(raw)} values: {raw}")


def start_session_server(args):
    """Start the standalone session servers when ``--use-session-server`` is set.

    One independent single-process server per resolved port; the rollout side
    picks one per session and its URL carries the affinity from then on.
    Always started standalone regardless of whether ``--use-miles-router`` is
    active.
    """
    if not getattr(args, "use_session_server", False):
        return

    hf_checkpoint = getattr(args, "hf_checkpoint", None)
    if not hf_checkpoint:
        raise ValueError("--use-session-server requires --hf-checkpoint to be set.")

    if getattr(args, "session_server_ip", None) is None:
        args.session_server_ip = args.sglang_router_ip

    ip = args.session_server_ip
    ports = _resolve_session_server_ports(getattr(args, "session_server_port", None))
    for port in ports:
        if not is_port_available(port):
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"Port {port} is already in use — a stale session server may still be running. "
                f"Run 'pkill -9 python' to kill it, then retry."
            )
    # The canonical driver-side value; rollout code picks from this list.
    args.session_server_ports = ports

    router_url = f"http://{args.sglang_router_ip}:{args.sglang_router_port}"

    # Spawn all children before waiting on any: each child pays the ~10s
    # transformers import, so N servers start in ~one import of wall-time.
    # spawn (not fork): see start_router for rationale.
    instance_ids: dict[int, str] = {}
    processes = []
    for port in ports:
        child_args = copy.copy(args)
        child_args.session_server_port = port
        child_args.session_server_instance_id = uuid.uuid4().hex
        instance_ids[port] = child_args.session_server_instance_id
        process = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process(
            target=run_session_server, args=(child_args, router_url)
        )
        process.daemon = True
        process.start()
        processes.append((port, process))
    # The per-port map OpenAIEndpointTracer.create reads instance ids from,
    # replacing the per-session /health probe.
    args.session_server_instance_ids = instance_ids
    for port, process in processes:
        wait_for_server_ready(ip, port, process, timeout=30)
    logger.info(
        "Session servers launched at %s, ports %s (%d instances), provider_paths=%s",
        ip,
        ports,
        len(ports),
        getattr(args, "session_provider_paths", None),
    )


def session_server_endpoints(args) -> list[tuple[str, int, str | None]]:
    """``(ip, port, instance_id)`` for every session server this driver started.

    Weight-update coordination is per process: each session server counts its
    own in-flight turns, so the trainer has to call ``/admin/quiesce`` on each
    one individually. Both pieces of state already exist on ``args`` after
    ``start_session_server``; this is the read path.
    """
    ports = getattr(args, "session_server_ports", None) or []
    instance_ids = getattr(args, "session_server_instance_ids", None) or {}
    ip = getattr(args, "session_server_ip", None) or getattr(args, "sglang_router_ip", None)
    return [(ip, port, instance_ids.get(port)) for port in ports]

steps.message: I found another concrete configuration/code mismatch: the launcher requests `consistent_hashing`, but `use_miles_router` selects Miles’ own proxy, whose scheduling code ignores the routing header and chooses the least-loaded worker on every request. That breaks the intended cross-turn cache affinity; it is separate from the stale-batch issue.
steps.reasoning_content: I found significant concrete bug: Miles router ignores policy entirely, least-active requests across turns. But is that root cause logs? Public prefix 46–52%, still decent; random turn routes lower affinity than consistent hashing. Historical performance perhaps Miles router similarly. Could be expected root cause multi: low rollout utilization due broken router cache affinity, async staleness missing. Should deeply analyze all possible roots. Summary initially said consistent_hashing per UUID routing keys, but I missed that Miles router proxy to engine URLs not actual SGLang router. It chooses min active count each call. Does SGLang engines have local radix cache and routing requests changing engine means prefix caches not reused across turns. Initial calls of different samples same base prompt get random route but cached if previous same. Turn n same trajectory not guaranteed. At low load, ties min picks first worker until active > other => first initial request engine0, next engine1, then both equal counts chooses 0, etc. For a sequential trajectory: call1 chooses worker0, call2 when call1 finished count all 0 chooses worker0 => affinity preserved! With concurrent load, selection can differ. Should compute from turn trace cached token data. Rerun avg cached prompt ratio 46%, still much better than historical b/c but not 97% a. The routing bug reduces cross-turn reuse. Is this root cause intended? I should establish with actual logs per-turn engine not directly recorded, but cache hit expected. Miles router clearly ignores header and requested policy. Could classify root of low cache hit and excess prefill, not of training stalls (historical remote semaphore). Should find original run log lines about worker selection perhaps "Using routing key" etc. Sanitized may hide. Search limited specific not all "router".

python3 -I - <<'PY'
import glob,json,collections,statistics,gzip
rows=[]
for f in glob.glob('logs/public_rerun/turns/*.jsonl.gz'):
 with gzip.open(f,'rt') as h: rows += [json.loads(x) for x in h]
g=collections.defaultdict(dict)
for r in rows:
 if r['event']=='generate':g[r['session']][r['turn']]=r
for t in range(1,7):
 vals=[]; hits=[]
 for sess,turns in g.items():
  if t in turns and t-1 in turns:
   prev,cur=turns[t-1],turns[t]
   avail=prev['prompt_tokens']+prev['completion_tokens']
   vals.append((cur['cached_tokens']-prev['cached_tokens'])/avail)
   hits.append((cur['cached_tokens'],prev['cached_tokens'],avail))
 print(t,'n',len(vals),'incremental_reuse mean',round(statistics.mean(vals),3),'median',round(statistics.median(vals),3),'p10/p90',round(sorted(vals)[len(vals)//10],3),round(sorted(vals)[len(vals)*9//10],3),'exact_or_better',sum(v>=.999 for v in vals)/len(vals),'negative',sum(v<0 for v in vals)/len(vals))

"""Rollout entrypoint: the fully-async producer plus a per-rollout summary.

``generate_rollout`` delegates to ``runtime.fully_async`` unchanged and then
writes ``rollout.<id>.json`` with the statistics a reviewer would pull from a
dashboard: accepted groups, rewards, response lengths, abort reasons and the
token-weighted prefix-cache hit rate reported by the inference engines.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import statistics
import time
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

from miles.utils.types import Sample

from .fully_async import generate_rollout_fully_async


def _flatten(groups):
    for group in groups:
        for item in group:
            if isinstance(item, list):
                yield from item
            else:
                yield item


def _summary(rollout_id: int, result, elapsed: float) -> dict:
    samples = list(_flatten(result.samples))
    rewards = [float(s.reward) for s in samples if s.reward is not None]
    cached = sum(s.prefix_cache_info.cached_tokens for s in samples)
    prompt = sum(s.prefix_cache_info.total_prompt_tokens for s in samples)
    lengths = [s.response_length for s in samples]
    return {
        "rollout_id": rollout_id,
        "wall_s": round(elapsed, 3),
        "groups": len(result.samples),
        "samples": len(samples),
        "status": dict(Counter(s.status.value if isinstance(s.status, Sample.Status) else str(s.status) for s in samples)),
        "reward_mean": statistics.fmean(rewards) if rewards else None,
        "reward_nonzero": sum(1 for r in rewards if r > 0),
        "response_length_mean": statistics.fmean(lengths) if lengths else None,
        "response_length_max": max(lengths) if lengths else None,
        "engine_prompt_tokens": prompt,
        "engine_cached_tokens": cached,
        "prefix_cache_hit_rate": cached / prompt if prompt else None,
        "abort_reasons": dict(Counter((s.metadata or {}).get("abort_reason") for s in samples if (s.metadata or {}).get("abort_reason"))),
        "metrics": {k: v for k, v in (result.metrics or {}).items() if isinstance(v, (int, float))},
    }


def generate_rollout(args, rollout_id, data_source, evaluation=False):
    started = time.time()
    result = generate_rollout_fully_async(args, rollout_id, data_source, evaluation=evaluation)
    record = _summary(rollout_id, result, time.time() - started)
    root = os.environ.get("RUN_EVIDENCE_DIR")
    if root:
        path = Path(root) / f"rollout.{rollout_id}.json"
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    print("ROLLOUT_SUMMARY " + json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True), flush=True)
    return result


generate_rollout.add_arguments = generate_rollout_fully_async.add_arguments

arguments.content:
# Diagnosis

**The setup runs, but it is not a healthy on-policy multi-turn GRPO pipeline.** Two concrete defects explain the suspicious metrics and poor rollout efficiency; neither is a failed checkpoint or a zero-gradient optimizer.

**1. Async staleness is accepted, then erased from the PPO ratio.** The launcher enables one-step overlap and per-step weight publication but supplies no behavior-policy correction (`scripts/train_reproduction.py:108-129`; `scripts/run_config.json:15-24,41-45`). The driver starts rollout `k+1` before training rollout `k` and publishing its weights (`runtime/source/train_async_entrypoint.py:59-67,89-93`), while the producer keeps 64 groups active and queues 64 completed groups, versus a training batch of only 16 (`runtime/fully_async.py:585-664`). `max_weight_staleness` is `None`, so the filter at `runtime/fully_async.py:797,909-938` never executes. Consequently all three accepted batches report `rollout/weight_version/{mean,min,max}=1` and `mixed_version_ratio=0`, despite weight updates after each step: steps 1 and 2 train on already-generated version-1 data, not the then-current actor. Batch 2 starts with `completed=96`, `queue_size=64`, accepts 16 groups in 0.037 s, and leaves 48 queued groups drained at shutdown. `mixed_version_ratio=0` only means no individual trajectory crossed versions; it does not mean the batch is fresh.

The configured loss then anchors PPO to the current actor rather than the policy that generated those trajectories. The resolved arguments are `use_rollout_logprobs=False`, `use_tis=False`, and no `keep_old_actor`; `vendor/miles/backends/training_utils/loss_hub/losses.py:118` therefore chooses the freshly recomputed `batch["log_probs"]` as `old_log_probs`. At the start of the single training pass the numerator and denominator are identical, giving the reported `ppo_kl=0`, `pg_clipfrac=0`, and `ess_ratio=1` on all three steps and making those diagnostics blind to rollout/actor mismatch. The actual engine-versus-training KL is nonzero (`0.00119`, `0.00140`, `0.00205`). In contrast, historical run-a explicitly logged `use_rollout_logprobs=True`, with step-42 `ppo_kl=0.09559` and `ess_ratio=0.531854`.

**2. The requested session cache affinity is silently discarded.** Configuration requests `use_miles_router=true` and `sglang_router_policy=consistent_hashing`, and generation assigns a stable per-sample UUID sent as `X-SMG-Routing-Key` on every turn (`vendor/miles/rollout/sglang_rollout.py:341-345`; `vendor/miles/rollout/generate_utils/generate_endpoint_utils.py:38-49`). But `use_miles_router` selects `MilesRouter` (`vendor/miles/ray/rollout/router_manager.py:35-41`); the policy is applied only in the other-router branch (`:43-53`). `MilesRouter` ignores that header and chooses the least-loaded worker for each request (`vendor/miles/router/router.py:129-153,215-230`). Successive turns can therefore land on different engines and recompute the conversation prefix. In the archived turn traces, 55.9% of 1,823 consecutive-turn transitions gained no cached tokens, and the median incremental prefix reuse was zero; the accepted-rollout prefix hit rates were only 46.3%, 49.9%, and 51.9%. This is a real cache-performance defect, not proof of wrong token content.

**Symptoms, not root causes.** The `1e-7`-scale scalar losses are signed batch means after within-group reward centering/std normalization, not zero gradients. All three rollouts returned 64/64 completed samples with no aborts, errors, truncation, or dynamic-filter drops; all 12 rank-level optimizer records report successful updates from the trainer. Grad norms were finite and nonzero (`0.7009`, `0.7767`, `0.7973`) with nonzero parameter deltas, so checkpoint conversion, weight transfer, and optimization are functioning. Rollout times of 78.1/10.1/0.037 s measure queue collection, not generation throughput; the final `rollout_idle_ratio=0.791` is the overlap/run-ahead consequence. Historical run-b/run-c had no logged training step and hundreds of long remote-sandbox semaphore waits, but that external environment and their deeper trajectories differ from this local rerun; those waits cannot be attributed to this workspace's tools. Dependency, Torch Dynamo, AccumulateGrad, NCCL-deprecation, and initial optional weight-session 400/404 messages are unrelated noise; subsequent weight updates and steps succeeded.

**Conclusion:** this short run proves mechanical liveness, not healthy learning. The demonstrated defects are unbounded, uncorrected stale-policy training and ineffective multi-turn cache affinity. Three steps and a slight accepted-reward decline (`0.9219→0.9109→0.9070`) are insufficient to establish long-term convergence damage or to attribute historical run-b/c stalls to these defects.

# Diagnosis

**The setup runs, but it is not a healthy on-policy multi-turn GRPO pipeline.** Two concrete defects explain the suspicious metrics and poor rollout efficiency; neither is a failed checkpoint or a zero-gradient optimizer.

**1. Async staleness is accepted, then erased from the PPO ratio.** The launcher enables one-step overlap and per-step weight publication but supplies no behavior-policy correction (`scripts/train_reproduction.py:108-129`; `scripts/run_config.json:15-24,41-45`). The driver starts rollout `k+1` before training rollout `k` and publishing its weights (`runtime/source/train_async_entrypoint.py:59-67,89-93`), while the producer keeps 64 groups active and queues 64 completed groups, versus a training batch of only 16 (`runtime/fully_async.py:585-664`). `max_weight_staleness` is `None`, so the filter at `runtime/fully_async.py:797,909-938` never executes. Consequently all three accepted batches report `rollout/weight_version/{mean,min,max}=1` and `mixed_version_ratio=0`, despite weight updates after each step: steps 1 and 2 train on already-generated version-1 data, not the then-current actor. Batch 2 starts with `completed=96`, `queue_size=64`, accepts 16 groups in 0.037 s, and leaves 48 queued groups drained at shutdown. `mixed_version_ratio=0` only means no individual trajectory crossed versions; it does not mean the batch is fresh.

The configured loss then anchors PPO to the current actor rather than the policy that generated those trajectories. The resolved arguments are `use_rollout_logprobs=False`, `use_tis=False`, and no `keep_old_actor`; `vendor/miles/backends/training_utils/loss_hub/losses.py:118` therefore chooses the freshly recomputed `batch["log_probs"]` as `old_log_probs`. At the start of the single training pass the numerator and denominator are identical, giving the reported `ppo_kl=0`, `pg_clipfrac=0`, and `ess_ratio=1` on all three steps and making those diagnostics blind to rollout/actor mismatch. The actual engine-versus-training KL is nonzero (`0.00119`, `0.00140`, `0.00205`). In contrast, historical run-a explicitly logged `use_rollout_logprobs=True`, with step-42 `ppo_kl=0.09559` and `ess_ratio=0.531854`.

**2. The requested session cache affinity is silently discarded.** Configuration requests `use_miles_router=true` and `sglang_router_policy=consistent_hashing`, and generation assigns a stable per-sample UUID sent as `X-SMG-Routing-Key` on every turn (`vendor/miles/rollout/sglang_rollout.py:341-345`; `vendor/miles/rollout/generate_utils/generate_endpoint_utils.py:38-49`). But `use_miles_router` selects `MilesRouter` (`vendor/miles/ray/rollout/router_manager.py:35-41`); the policy is applied only in the other-router branch (`:43-53`). `MilesRouter` ignores that header and chooses the least-loaded worker for each request (`vendor/miles/router/router.py:129-153,215-230`). Successive turns can therefore land on different engines and recompute the conversation prefix. In the archived turn traces, 55.9% of 1,823 consecutive-turn transitions gained no cached tokens, and the median incremental prefix reuse was zero; the accepted-rollout prefix hit rates were only 46.3%, 49.9%, and 51.9%. This is a real cache-performance defect, not proof of wrong token content.

**Symptoms, not root causes.** The `1e-7`-scale scalar losses are signed batch means after within-group reward centering/std normalization, not zero gradients. All three rollouts returned 64/64 completed samples with no aborts, errors, truncation, or dynamic-filter drops; all 12 rank-level optimizer records report successful updates from the trainer. Grad norms were finite and nonzero (`0.7009`, `0.7767`, `0.7973`) with nonzero parameter deltas, so checkpoint conversion, weight transfer, and optimization are functioning. Rollout times of 78.1/10.1/0.037 s measure queue collection, not generation throughput; the final `rollout_idle_ratio=0.791` is the overlap/run-ahead consequence. Historical run-b/run-c had no logged training step and hundreds of long remote-sandbox semaphore waits, but that external environment and their deeper trajectories differ from this local rerun; those waits cannot be attributed to this workspace's tools. Dependency, Torch Dynamo, AccumulateGrad, NCCL-deprecation, and initial optional weight-session 400/404 messages are unrelated noise; subsequent weight updates and steps succeeded.

**Conclusion:** this short run proves mechanical liveness, not healthy learning. The demonstrated defects are unbounded, uncorrected stale-policy training and ineffective multi-turn cache affinity. Three steps and a slight accepted-reward decline (`0.9219→0.9109→0.9070`) are insufficient to establish long-term convergence damage or to attribute historical run-b/c stalls to these defects.
